best_for: Scientists, analysts and students coming from MATLAB or RStudio who want to run Python line by line and inspect their data as they go.

points.title: Built for data work
points.text: An editor, IPython consoles, plots and a variable explorer sit side by side. You can open NumPy arrays and pandas tables in a grid to check them, much like a MATLAB workspace.

points.title: Debugger and profiler included
points.text: Static analysis, an interactive debugger, a profiler, project support and find-in-files come with it, so you rarely need another tool.

points.title: Free, MIT licensed
points.text: Spyder is free and open source under the MIT license, funded by donations and groups including NumFOCUS and the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative.

points.title: Standalone installer has limits
points.text: The installers bundle Python with NumPy, SciPy, pandas and Matplotlib and update themselves. To use other packages, point Spyder at a separate Python. Third-party plugins and full Variable Explorer support for libraries like PyTorch need a Conda install.

points.title: Conda is the safer route
points.text: The docs recommend installing Spyder into its own Conda environment through Miniforge, and warn that Anaconda's bundled copy is often out of date.

points.title: A heavy Flatpak
points.text: The Flathub build is community-made and not verified by the Spyder team. It downloads about 580 MB and lags behind at 6.1.6 against 6.1.8 on Windows and Mac.

points.title: Installers and versions
points.text: Windows offers per-user and machine-wide x64 installers, and the listing keeps 51 versions. Mac gets separate Intel and Apple silicon .pkg installers. macOS and Linux list only the current release.
